text: Hi everyone, and welcome to RFC Legends! We built it at ETHGlobal Tokyo twenty twenty-six. It's an idle rooster adventure, and the birds behind it carry farm-signed records onchain. I'll show you where it comes from, how it works, and exactly what we built for World, ENS and Curvegrid.

RFC began at Ninlanee Farm in Thailand, where Thai fighting roosters are raised. The dream is big: raise the standard of Thai cockfighting and take it worldwide, with new universal rules that turn it into an international sport. Think of what ONE Championship did for Muay Thai.

From the farm, RFC grew into an ecosystem: the RFC Club app, RFC TV, and our multimedia channels. Now we're building RFC NFT, a real-world asset that maps each rooster on the farm to the blockchain, launching soon for selling roosters digitally. And RFC's AI scoring aims to judge results to one fair standard.

RFC Legends is the game for RFC NFT holders: a place to play, build community and connect. What you'll see today is live: an idle adventure with your rooster, rare drops, guild chat and a shared guild boss, and a market where players trade drops. Next come holder privileges, breeding new bloodlines, and dressing up your rooster and trainer.

Here's how it works. A server-authoritative TypeScript engine runs every combat tick and settles offline rewards, with PocketBase holding player state, guild chat and the guild boss. Rare items and rooster records live in five contracts on Sepolia, and World ID, ENS version two and Curvegrid MultiBaas handle proof of human, pedigree and indexing.

This is the loop in our demo. A boss drops a rare card. The player proves they're human with World ID, and our server signs an EIP-712 voucher, so the card mints as an ERC-1155 item. It's listed in the Rare Market, a buyer pays, and the contract splits ninety-ten between seller and treasury in one transaction. Then the refusals: an unverified bot, and a second wallet of the same human.

For World, IDKit gates the whole economy. The widget proves personhood, and our server verifies the proof with the signal pinned to the player's wallet and a one-time nonce, so it can't be replayed. The nullifier is bound to one wallet and mirrored onchain in HumanRegistry, which the mint and the market both check before any value moves.

Our first IDKit line to a live verify took sixty-two minutes. The friction was an undocumented staging token, a simulator that ignored our connect link, and a simulator with a single identity worldwide. Our top request for World: let the Portal reject a reused nullifier per action, and check the signal a proof was made for.

For ENS, the name is the pedigree. Offspring live as subnames inside their sire's own registry, so chick zero one dot theprawang is a real child of its sire onchain. A permissioned resolver decides who writes what: only the farm's key can write health records, while the namespace owner handles bloodline fields. Our rooster pages resolve it all live.

For Curvegrid, every rooster token needs two parties. The issuer submits the mint, and the farm co-signs the leg-ring ID, bloodline and hatch date, so nobody invents a bird alone. The farm signs health attestations that anyone can relay onchain. All five contracts are indexed in MultiBaas, and the market's ninety-ten sale history comes straight from a saved Sold-event query.

Everything onchain here was written during ETHGlobal Tokyo: five contracts verified on Etherscan and Sourcify, a hundred and five Foundry tests at one hundred percent line coverage, and a live demo on Sepolia. Our World ID work started at seven thirty-seven UTC on day one, and MultiBaas indexing was wired up live during the event.

That's RFC Legends. You can play it right now at rfclegends dot rfcclub dot app, and every contract, pointer and transaction is in our GitHub repo. Thank you World, ENS and Curvegrid, and thank you for watching!
